title: Rigging with layer parenting
summary: Rig a character's arm and hand to its body with layer parenting, pose the rig, and choose what the children take on from their parents.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text:
In this lesson you will rig a simple character with layer parenting: the hand follows the arm and the arm follows the body, the way a forearm follows the upper arm.

The document is ready: the body, the arm and the hand are symbol instances on layers of their own. Click Next to begin.

steps.title: Parent the arm to the body
steps.text:
Right-click the Arm layer's name and choose Parent Layer > Body.

Nothing moves yet: the arm stays where it is, but from now on it follows the body.

steps.title: Parent the hand to the arm
steps.text:
Right-click the Hand layer's name and choose Parent Layer > Arm. The hand now follows the arm, and through it the body.

The linked-circles button at the top right of the layer list shows the links as lines, and lets you drag a layer's handle onto its parent instead.

steps.title: Move the body
steps.text: Press V for the Selection tool and drag the body across the stage. The arm and the hand come along.

steps.title: Pick the Free Transform tool
steps.text: Press Q, or click the Free Transform tool in the toolbox.

steps.title: Raise the arm
steps.text: Click the arm to select it. Then drag from just outside a corner handle of its box to rotate it, so the arm points up. It turns at the shoulder, where its transformation point is, and the hand turns with it.

steps.title: Lean the body
steps.text: Click the body and rotate it a little the same way. The whole rig leans together: the arm keeps its pose and the hand stays on the end of it.

steps.title: Scale the body
steps.text: With the body selected, drag a corner handle outward to make it bigger. The arm and the hand grow with it, as children take on their parent's scale by default.

steps.title: Choose what the arm follows
steps.text:
Right-click the Arm layer's name and choose Properties.... Under Follow parent's, uncheck Scale and click OK.

A child always follows its parent's position and rotation; Scale, Skew and Flip are yours to choose. The arm may change size on the stage, as it no longer takes on the body's scale.

steps.title: Scale the body again
steps.text: Select the body and scale it again. Now the arm and the hand still move and turn with it, but keep their size.

steps.title: Well done
steps.text:
You rigged a body, arm and hand with layer parenting, posed the rig by moving and rotating the parents, and chose which parts of a parent's transform a child follows.

To set a layer free, choose Parent Layer > None. Help > Tutorials has more lessons, such as Motion tweens and the Motion Editor.
